newsitem.title: POLAND: PROCHEM SAYS FLUOR DANIEL MAY CALL TENDER.
newsitem.headline: PROCHEM SAYS FLUOR DANIEL MAY CALL TENDER.

text.p: Fluor Corp subsidiary Fluor Daniel BV, which currently controls 32.81 percent of Polish engineering firm Prochem SA, may be soon be forced to call a public tender offer, Prochem's deputy head.

Marek Garlinski told Reuters on Thursday that if more Prochem shareholders who hold preferred registered shares entitling to three votes each convert them to common shares, Fluor Daniel could gain 33-percent control of the firm.
Fluor holds 35 percent of the firm's shares.

But Garlinski said his firm had agreed with Fluor Daniel that any public tender offer, which under Polish law is required of shareholders gaining 33-percent control of a firm, would be at a price low enough to quash supply.
"If there's a tender no one will respond because the price will be low -- Fluor doesn't want to raise its stake that way," Garlinski said.

He said that though there was no immediate plan for Fluor to raise it stake, it would normally do so through a capital raise, and could conceivably take up shares if Prochem issued them during a period of low demand.

Garlinski said Prochem was mulling an issue of new shares or convertible bonds next year but that this would depend on whether the firm needed extra funds to finance its programme to invest 30 million zlotys to add firms to its holding.
